response.justification: The candidate is an experienced, versatile senior engineer with strong full-stack, testing, and open-source credentials, but the profile diverges sharply from the role's core requirements. The job demands 8 years of C++ programming and 5 years building large-scale infrastructure/compute platforms; the resume shows only ~6 months of C/C++ work at National Instruments (2014-2015) and a university thesis project, with C++ absent from the listed skills. Low-latency, high-throughput distributed systems experience exists (Dunnhumby/Sociomantic, in D rather than C++), and there is DevOps/Kubernetes exposure, but no internal cloud compute platform ownership. Technical leadership is evidenced through mentoring, workshops, and founding an open-source project, though not as a formal team technical lead for cloud/DevOps engineers. Overall, the C++ and large-scale cloud compute gaps are disqualifying for this specific role.
strengths: Proven low-latency, high-throughput systems work (millions of req/sec at Sociomantic)
Strong mentoring, teaching, and community leadership track record (workshops, courses, talks)
Broad polyglot engineering plus DevOps/CI/CD, Docker, and Kubernetes experience
concerns: Only ~6 months of professional C++ experience versus the 8-year minimum
No production cloud compute platform or hardware/storage architecture ownership
Recent work is product/web-focused (TypeScript/Node), not systems infrastructure leadership
